reasons: Missing-clause finding is well supported: the only cited neighbouring text (Section 14.12 risk of loss) addresses allocation of risk, not coverage, and the rationale reports no 'insur' hits anywhere in the document, so no usable insurance clause exists.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook's model language at the preferred position (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M for Customer Data, workers' comp, certificates on request) and correctly names IBM (vendor) as the insuring party, with the customer bearing no new obligation.
Placement in the general/miscellaneous area after the risk-of-loss provision follows the redline guidance, and the insertion is additive so no existing customer-favourable language is disturbed.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, prefixed, accurately explains the gap and the rationale (IBM hosts and processes our data), states the playbook position and offers the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback.
Deterministic checks all pass; the high changed-character ratio is inherent to an insertion-type finding and is not a defect here.
